title: docs(types): the two i18n label vocabularies refuse each other, measured (objectui#9375)
body:
Fixes #9375

Clause-②: no

The vocabulary prose on `BaseSchema` said the two i18n label shapes "each accept the other's shape vacuously". Measured against the tree, that is false in both directions — and the `label` docblock one property over was saying the same thing in its own words, so both are corrected here. Comment-only: no declaration, accept set or requiredness moves, per objectui#9092's read-only fence on `BaseSchema`.

## 1. The instrument first — does it discriminate?

The card rests on `packages/types/src/__tests__/inline-locale-declared-face-9092.test.ts` (added by objectui#9364). Taken on its own word, a green run proves nothing: the file's `tsc` half is read only by `tsc -p packages/types/tsconfig.test.json`, and an `@ts-expect-error` on a line that the compiler would never flag is itself an error, so the baseline zero had to be lit before it could be read.

Three ablations, each proved to have reached the disk (marker counts before/after + `git hash-object` against the HEAD blob), each restored with `git checkout HEAD --` and `git diff HEAD` proved empty, all under a trapped script:

| direction | ablation | exit | what tsc printed |
|---|---|---|---|
| refusal is real (keyed slot) | drop the directive over `ariaLabel: LOCALE_MAP` | 2 | `(172,49): error TS2322: Type 'Record...&{key?: undefined; defaultValue?: undefined;}' is not assignable to type 'string | KeyedI18nLabel | undefined'` |
| refusal is real (inline slot) | drop the directive over `ObjectGridSchema.label: KEYED_REF` | 2 | `(159,83): error TS2322: Type '{ key: string; defaultValue: string; }' is not assignable to ...` |
| it can also tell ACCEPT apart | add a directive over the line that must compile (`ariaLabel: KEYED_REF`) | 2 | `(178,5): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.` |

Baseline with all three restored: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 0, `vitest` 10/10. The third row is the one that matters most: the instrument is not a slot that refuses every object — it distinguishes the two vocabularies.

## 2. Then the same two crossings, measured on `BaseSchema` itself

The instrument asserts the inline crossings on inheritors (`ObjectGridSchema`, `AppComponentSchema`, `PageNodeSchema.aria`) and the keyed crossing on the flat slot. Since the docblock being corrected is `BaseSchema`'s own, both crossings were re-measured directly on `BaseSchema`, in a throwaway probe that was deleted afterwards (worktree proved clean):

- `tsc`: `label: KEYED`, `description: KEYED` and `ariaLabel: MAP` each fire an `@ts-expect-error`; `label/description: MAP` and `ariaLabel: KEYED` compile as controls. Exit 0 with all five present.
- parse (`zod/base.zod.ts#BaseSchema`): `safeParse` is `false` for the same three crossings and `true` for the same two controls.

Mechanism, read off the installed pin rather than assumed: `InlineLocaleMapSchema` is typed `Record<string, string> & { key?: never; defaultValue?: never }`, and the refusal message names the pattern `^(?!(?:key|defaultValue)$)(default|[A-Za-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*)$`.

## 3. What a wrong slot actually costs — also measured, not quoted

Against the installed pin, with controls:

- `resolveI18nLabel({ key: 'a.b', defaultValue: 'D' }, 'en')` returns `"a.b"` — the key renders. Control: `resolveI18nLabel({ en: 'Accounts', 'fr-FR': 'Comptes' }, 'en')` returns `"Accounts"`; `resolveI18nLabel(42, 'en')` returns `undefined`.
- `resolveKeyedI18nLabel({ en: 'Owner' })` returns `undefined` — the aria-label renders empty. Control: `resolveKeyedI18nLabel({ key: 'a.b', defaultValue: 'D' })` returns `"D"`.

So the residual hazard is a WRONG ANSWER, paid by metadata that reaches a resolver without passing either face — the normal case for server-driven JSON — and not the vacuous acceptance the prose claimed.

## 4. Sentences changed

**A. `BaseSchema.ariaLabel`, the sentence the card names.**

- before: "Two properties apart, both spelled `string | {object}`, and each accepts the other's shape vacuously. Check which resolver owns a slot before writing an object into it; the ruling accepted this cost with exactly this naming + cross-referencing as the mitigation."
- after: "Two properties apart, both spelled `string | {object}` — but NEITHER SLOT ADMITS THE OTHER'S SHAPE. The installed pin types the inline arm with `key?: never; defaultValue?: never` and its `INLINE_LOCALE_KEY` pattern excludes both names, so a keyed ref written into `label` / `description`, and an inline map written into this slot, are each REFUSED — at `tsc` on the declaration and at `safeParse` on the zod mirror. The cross-vocabulary block of `__tests__/inline-locale-declared-face-9092.test.ts` re-derives that on every run, in both directions and with the accepting control beside each refusal; read it rather than this sentence." Followed by a new paragraph carrying the wrong-answer cost measured in section 3, and keeping the original advice ("check which resolver owns a slot") and the ruling's mitigation clause verbatim.

**B. `BaseSchema.label` — the other half of the same claim, which the card did not name.** This is the correction that would have been missed by fixing only the named sentence.

- before: "they are structurally confusable: a keyed ref typed into this slot is accepted only *vacuously*, as a locale map whose "locales" are named `key` and `defaultValue`."
- after: "they stay confusable to a READER — but NOT to the compiler or the parser: a keyed ref written into this slot is REFUSED, because the installed pin types the inline arm with `key?: never; defaultValue?: never` and its `INLINE_LOCALE_KEY` pattern excludes both names." Plus a pointer to `ariaLabel` for the full statement.

**C. The `NOT I18nLabel` paragraph on `ariaLabel` — marked as history rather than rewritten.** PR #4593's three measurements were correct about the spelling the ruling withdrew, so they stay; what changed is that they no longer read as the current reading.

- before: "...withdrew it (#4580 Q2-B): `I18nLabel` is the spec's INLINE LOCALE MAP (`string | Record<string, string>`), so the shipped keyed fixture was accepted only *vacuously*..."
- after: "...withdrew it (#4580 Q2-B). Read those three as HISTORY, against the `I18nLabel` of that release — `string | Record<string, string>`, a map with no name excluded from it: the shipped keyed fixture was accepted *vacuously*, ... The pin has since closed the vacuous half — see below. What survives is that the two vocabularies are structurally confusable to a READER — objectui#4167's exact hazard."

**D. Two spellings of the inline arm, which were the premise the refuted claim rested on.** The file-level `KeyedI18nLabel` vocabulary block and the `label` docblock both spelled the spec's inline form `string | Record<string, string>` flat — a spelling under which `{ key, defaultValue }` IS a member, which is exactly what made "accepted vacuously" readable as current. Both now carry the pin's exclusion (`key?: never; defaultValue?: never`). No other wording in those paragraphs moves.

**E. One line address removed.** The `ariaLabel` docblock cited `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:111`; the call is at line 126 on `origin/main`. The quoted code is unchanged and still correct, so the citation now names the file and the symbol and drops the number — a number in published prose is a claim with a shelf life, and `check:new-line-citations` reports on exactly this shape.

Whole-repo `pnpm lint` and the rest of the gate farm are left to CI.

Published-bytes check, on the final commit: after building, `dist/base.d.ts` carries the corrected sentence and no longer carries the old one — which is why the changeset is a `patch` rather than an empty declaration.

## 6. Pending-changeset re-read (the `changeset-claim-re-read` gate)

The gate listed 11 pending changesets whose bodies name `packages/types/src/base.ts`. It is report-only and judges name resolution, not meaning; the meaning question is answered here. **Verdict: none of the 11 goes false, and one of them is independently corroborated by this PR's measurements. No pending body is edited.**

**The decisive property, re-derived here on two instruments against merge-base `78a9c6744`.**

- Line level: of the changed lines in `base.ts`, 0 are non-comment. Every `+`/`-` line matches `^[+-] +\*`.
- Whole file: with comments stripped, both sides hash identically — `sha256[:16] = 1d8d2a4a9d1ed76f`, 3202 bytes each. **Lit control:** renaming one declared key (`ariaLabel` to `ariaLabelX`) in the head copy and re-stripping gives `122f6229754cf290`, so the hash is capable of telling a declaration change apart from a comment change.
- Block level: of the 77 JSDoc blocks in the file, exactly 3 changed bytes, and they document `KeyedI18nLabel` (L22), `BaseSchema.label` (L91, `label?: string | I18nLabel`) and `BaseSchema.ariaLabel` (L465). Every other block is byte-identical, including `ComponentInput`, `ComponentMeta`, `StyleProps`, `children`, `inputType`, `defaultValue`, `description`, and the `label?: never` member of `ComponentInput` at L733 — a different `label` from the one this PR edits.

⇒ A pending claim can only go false here if it asserts something about the text of those three docblocks. Claims about members, retirement kits (`?: never` + `retirementTombstone()`), mirrors, re-exports or parity are untouched by construction, and the block-level reading is what makes that a measurement rather than an argument.

**The one the gate's reader is right to single out: `.changeset/7088-hidden-jsdoc-single-hide-path.md`.** It is a claim about comment text in this very file, so the comment-only argument does not dispose of it. Read in full, its subject is `BaseSchema.hidden`'s JSDoc and the sibling `visible` comment (plus the schema-reference `hidden` row and `SchemaRenderer.hiddenVisibleSynonymy.test.tsx`, neither in this diff). Measured: the `hidden`, `visible`, `visibleWhen`, `visibleOn` and `hiddenOn` JSDoc blocks are byte-identical between merge-base and this branch, and no sentence of 7088's body names `label`, `ariaLabel`, `KeyedI18nLabel`, `I18nLabel` or i18n at all (0 hits for that token set; `base.ts` resolves as the lit control). Its general sentence — "the JSDoc is the authority a later docs correction is measured against" — is not disputed by this change either: 7088 itself backs its JSDoc with a pin test, and this PR moves a JSDoc toward what an instrument re-derives, which is the same direction. **Still true.**

**`.changeset/zod-base-schema-mirror-parity-4605.md` — the one this PR corroborates.** It says `label`/`description` take the spec's inline map and `ariaLabel` the keyed reference, that "each slot admits only its own vocabulary and both cross pairings are pinned as rejections", and that `resolveKeyedI18nLabel` "returns `undefined` for a locale map and would render an EMPTY aria-label". Both sentences were re-measured for this PR (section 2 and section 3) and both hold. **Still true — and it is the pending body that already said what the docblock is only now catching up to.**

**The other nine.** Verified rather than inherited: each was scanned for any token of the changed docblocks' subject, with `base.ts` as the lit control for the scanner. Two produced a hit and were read: `5928-classname-style-props-rename` uses "vocabulary" of `StyleProps`' Tailwind scale (that block is byte-identical), and `componentinput-reexport-4972` uses it of `ComponentInputControlType` (likewise). The remaining seven — `5905-componentinput-inputtype-tombstone`, `5905-componentinput-retire-constraint-keys`, `6067-component-meta-derive-from-canonical`, `7493-componentinput-retire-label-defaultvalue-advanced`, `component-meta-converge-and-deprecate-alias-5893`, `default-children-retired-5051`, `plugin-component-input-deprecate-5674` — are about declarations, retirement kits and re-exports, and name none of the three changed blocks. **All still true.**

## Acceptance notes

Found and deliberately NOT done:

- `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` says "neither resolver **accepts** the other's shape" — true of the two resolvers' signatures, misleading about runtime for the reason measured in section 3. The card names this sibling explicitly as a different claim; that file is also the surface of open PR objectui#9709, so it is left untouched. Noted, not filed — the card already records it.
- `packages/{components,core,plugin-dashboard,react,types}/CHANGELOG.md` each carry the old sentence in a released entry. Release records are history and are never rewritten. A whitespace-tolerant scan of the whole tree (the prose wraps near eighty columns, so a line-anchored matcher is blind to it) found no other LIVE copy: `packages/types/src/app.ts` and the instrument's own header were already corrected by objectui#9364.
- `packages/types/src/base.ts` has two other cross-file line citations of the same rotting shape (`.../bridges/list-view.ts:180` and `:224`, in the `label` and `description` docblocks). Not verified and not touched — outside the vocabulary claim this card is about. Noted, not filed; the handler is whoever next edits those two docblocks, and `check:new-line-citations` already reports the class.
